goal: Complete the existing one-window access UI for ordinary/protected roles, role creation, and server-owned access-editor handoff without redesigning navigation or duplicating write paths.
acceptance: The existing one-window slices and left/right sidebar mechanics remain intact.
AccessWorkspaceView remains the canonical editor and the only workspace write adapter; no duplicate user or role mutation service is introduced for AI or global-panel rendering.

The workspace right editor remains a Kanban-style overlay. A server-owned access.open_editor command renders the same user or role editor as an HTMX fragment in #global-right-panel-content, never a complete HTML document, and Save stays inside the drawer without a document reload.
Standalone user and role URLs remain usable as reserve new-tab routes, while their normal links do not become a second navigation hierarchy.
Ordinary and protected roles and denial reasons are clear.

The Roles cut contains an obvious Create role action. An authorized administrator creates an ordinary role in the right overlay, then edits and assigns it without leaving the workspace; protected creation remains superuser-only and is visibly explained.
Site sections remain read-only projections and advanced identity or memory fields do not appear as role grants.
Role rows visibly distinguish ordinary and protected roles without relying only on color; protected-role assignment and edit denials are shown next to the unavailable action.

Desktop and 320px narrow-screen Save, dirty-close confirmation, server validation errors, Escape/focus behavior, left-sidebar resizing/chat restoration, access.open_editor rendering, and absence of full document reload pass browser e2e.
All HTMX/fetch requests are bounded; timeout or transport failure clears busy state and preserves the dirty draft with a retryable error.
The owner records explicit UI acceptance before final merge.

architecture.canonical_write_path: AccessWorkspaceView delegates to the existing account/role services; fragments must not bypass them.
architecture.right_panel: Use the existing drawer/overlay behavior and #global-right-panel-content for server-owned handoff. The provider resolves a canonical workspace query from trusted target type/id; callers cannot supply a URL or HTML target.
architecture.role_creation: Treat create-role as an explicit workspace editor state with a blank ordinary-role form. On success, render the newly created role definition in the same right overlay and refresh the Roles table out-of-band when that table exists.
architecture.standalone_routes: Keep current full-page GET/POST routes as reserve paths; shared partials or helpers may be extracted, but mutation logic remains service-backed and identical.
architecture.responsive: Desktop uses the overlay drawer above the workspace; at narrow width it occupies the viewport. The left field editor remains in the sidebar location on desktop and becomes a floating layer only on narrow screens.
security_invariants: Fresh actor authorization is rechecked by existing services at save time.
Role base_hash and user base_version/CAS semantics remain mandatory where currently defined.
Only ordinary role creation is delegated; a protected role can be created, edited, or assigned only by an active superuser.
Site-section, technical-group, and memory-group projections do not become role capability grants.
No preview/confirmation token or risk checkbox is reintroduced.
non_goals: No navigation redesign beyond the existing six cuts.
No capability-catalog or role-contract schema change.
No AI write tool and no generic arbitrary edit panel.
No change to the Django Admin reserve path.
